title: CSS modules/tooling as future awareness only
learningObjectives: Explain css modules/tooling as future awareness only and implement a maintainable CSS workflow or lab.

understand.concept: CSS Modules and build tooling can scope class names or transform styles during a build. They are optional project tools, not browser CSS features. A browser ultimately receives CSS that it can parse and apply.
understand.whyItMatters: Tooling can help large projects avoid naming collisions, but it adds a build pipeline and conventions. Beginners should understand native CSS first and adopt tooling only when project scale justifies it.
understand.analogy: A build tool is a preparation step that organises source materials before the browser receives the finished stylesheet.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the design; implementation must follow browser APIs, CSS behaviour, and accessibility requirements.

explain.narrative: The example uses ordinary browser CSS. CSS Modules would transform local class names during a build, but the browser still receives CSS.

practise.guidedTask: Explain the difference between native CSS and a build-time CSS Modules workflow. Identify what the browser receives at runtime.
practise.independentTask: Build a small production-minded example. Validate input, keep the baseline usable, and document browser and accessibility checks.
hints: Keep one canonical state for synchronized controls.
